name: Chat Demo Panel
summary: A cropped chat or agent panel plays a scripted conversation: messages pop in one at a time, the assistant's answer streams in, and the thread scrolls up as it grows. It is the longer demo scene that shows the product actually doing the work.
when_to_use: Demonstrating an AI assistant or support agent answering a real request.
Showing reasoning steps or tool calls alongside a conversation.
Walking through a multi-turn exchange that ends in a resolved outcome.

slots.name: panel_chrome
slots.what: the chat window or panel frame, cropped and placed on a branded background

slots.name: messages
slots.what: a short scripted list of user and assistant turns in plain language

slots.name: answer_body
slots.what: the assistant's longest reply, as bullets or short lines that stream in

slots.name: source_chips
slots.what: optional small chips or citations appended to answer lines

slots.name: side_panel
slots.what: an optional card beside the chat showing reasoning steps or a mascot

slots.name: avatars
slots.what: small avatars marking who is speaking

steps: The panel slides or pushes into frame over the background, sometimes opened by a cursor click.
The user's message types on or pops in as a bubble.
The assistant's reply streams in line by line, with chips or status rows appended as it goes.
Older bubbles scroll up and out behind a mask as new turns arrive.
An optional side card fills in step with each assistant turn.
The exchange ends on the resolved outcome before a cut.

build.gsap: One timeline per scene built from a scripted message array. For each turn, pop the bubble in with a small scale-up and fade on a back or expo ease-out, then tween the inner thread container's y inside an overflow-hidden mask so the stack scrolls up. Stream answer lines with a stagger on opacity and a short upward move, or reveal them left to right with a gradient mask tween, and pop each chip right after its line. Drive the side card's bullets with the same timeline labels so they land with each assistant turn. A slow scale on the panel wrapper gives the gentle camera push.
build.remotion: One Sequence per turn, offset by the script's timing. Inside each, a stiff spring drives the bubble's scale and opacity, and a damped spring drives the thread's scroll offset. Stream answer lines with staggered springs or an interpolated mask width, and render the side card from the same turn index.

sound: Music carries most of the scene. Reversed swooshes and impacts tend to come later, as panels or answers land deep into the scene rather than at its start; a pop or click occasionally marks a single bubble or a send. Many cues are unclassified.
caveats: Sound counts are dominated by a few long shots from a handful of videos, so cue offsets mostly reflect those shots.
One member is a real screen recording and another is several scenes merged into one shot, so lengths vary widely.
